categories.title: Foundations
categories.description: Sorting basics, divide-and-conquer, recurrences and probabilistic analysis (Part I).

algorithms.title: Insertion Sort
algorithms.summary: Builds a sorted prefix by inserting each element into place; the book's first algorithm.

algorithms.title: Linear Search
algorithms.summary: Scan until the value is found; a loop-invariant warm-up exercise.

algorithms.title: Selection Sort
algorithms.summary: Repeatedly select the minimum of the unsorted suffix and swap it forward.

algorithms.title: Merge Sort
algorithms.summary: Divide-and-conquer sort: split, sort halves recursively, merge in linear time.

algorithms.title: Bubble Sort
algorithms.summary: Swap adjacent out-of-order pairs; simple, correct, and Θ(n²).

algorithms.title: Binary Search
algorithms.summary: Halve a sorted search interval each step: Θ(lg n). Includes the two-sum-in-sorted-order idea.

algorithms.title: Horner's Rule
algorithms.summary: Evaluate a degree-n polynomial with n multiplications and n additions.

algorithms.title: Counting Inversions
algorithms.summary: Count out-of-order pairs in Θ(n lg n) by augmenting merge sort.

algorithms.title: Maximum Subarray
algorithms.summary: Divide-and-conquer (and Kadane's linear scan) for the contiguous subarray of maximum sum.

algorithms.title: Matrix Multiplication (Naive & Recursive)
algorithms.summary: Θ(n³) triple loop and the Θ(n³) divide-and-conquer version on n/2 × n/2 blocks.

algorithms.title: Strassen's Algorithm
algorithms.summary: Seven recursive half-size products instead of eight: Θ(n^lg 7) ≈ Θ(n^2.81).

algorithms.title: Master Theorem
algorithms.summary: Solve T(n)=aT(n/b)+Θ(n^k·lg^p n) by comparing the watershed n^(log_b a) with the driving function.

algorithms.title: Akra–Bazzi Recurrence Method
algorithms.summary: Solves recurrences with unequal subproblem sizes: find p with Σ aᵢ·bᵢ^p = 1, then integrate.

algorithms.title: Hiring Problem & Indicator Variables
algorithms.summary: HIRE-ASSISTANT and its expected number of hires (the harmonic number H_n ≈ ln n).

algorithms.title: Random Permutations & Sampling
algorithms.summary: PERMUTE-BY-SORTING, RANDOMIZE-IN-PLACE, random subsets, and RANDOM(a,b) from fair coin flips.

algorithms.title: Online Hiring (Secretary Problem)
algorithms.summary: Observe the first k=n/e candidates, then hire the first one who beats them: success ≈ 1/e.

algorithms.title: Birthday Paradox, Balls & Bins, Streaks
algorithms.summary: The probabilistic-analysis examples: birthday collisions, coupon collector, longest streak of heads.

categories.title: Sorting & Order Statistics
categories.description: Heaps, quicksort, linear-time sorts, sorting networks and selection (Part II).

algorithms.title: Heapsort
algorithms.summary: MAX-HEAPIFY, BUILD-MAX-HEAP and in-place Θ(n lg n) heapsort.

algorithms.title: Priority Queue (Binary Heap)
algorithms.summary: INSERT, MAXIMUM, EXTRACT-MAX, INCREASE-KEY and DELETE on a heap; also merging k sorted lists.

algorithms.title: d-ary Heap
algorithms.summary: A heap whose nodes have d children: shallower tree, cheaper INSERT, costlier EXTRACT-MAX.

algorithms.title: Young Tableaux
algorithms.summary: A sorted m×n matrix acting as a priority queue: EXTRACT-MIN in O(m+n), sorting n² numbers in O(n³).

algorithms.title: Quicksort
algorithms.summary: Partition around a pivot (Lomuto scheme) and recurse: Θ(n lg n) expected, Θ(n²) worst case.

algorithms.title: Hoare Partition Quicksort
algorithms.summary: The original two-pointer partition scheme: fewer swaps than Lomuto.

algorithms.title: Randomized Quicksort
algorithms.summary: Pick the pivot uniformly at random: expected Θ(n lg n) on every input.

algorithms.title: Quicksort Variants
algorithms.summary: Three-way partitioning for equal keys, tail-recursion elimination with O(lg n) stack, median-of-3 pivots.

algorithms.title: Stooge Sort
algorithms.summary: A deliberately slow recursive sort: Θ(n^(lg 3/lg 1.5)) ≈ Θ(n^2.71).

algorithms.title: Counting Sort
algorithms.summary: Stable Θ(n+k) sort for integer keys in 0..=k, using a prefix-sum table.

algorithms.title: Radix Sort
algorithms.summary: Sort d-digit keys with d passes of a stable sort, least-significant digit first.

algorithms.title: Bucket Sort
algorithms.summary: Distribute uniform keys in [0,1) into n buckets, sort each by insertion sort: Θ(n) expected.

algorithms.title: Comparison Networks & the 0-1 Principle
algorithms.summary: Fixed sequences of compare-exchange gates; test any network exhaustively on 0-1 inputs.

algorithms.title: Bitonic Sorting Network
algorithms.summary: Half-cleaners turn a bitonic sequence into two bitonic halves; depth lg n·(lg n+1)/2.

algorithms.title: Odd-Even Merging Network
algorithms.summary: Batcher's odd-even merge sort: merge by recursively merging odd and even subsequences.

algorithms.title: Simultaneous Minimum and Maximum
algorithms.summary: Find both extremes with at most 3⌊n/2⌋ comparisons by pairing elements.

algorithms.title: Randomized Select
algorithms.summary: Quickselect: find the i-th smallest element in expected Θ(n) time.

algorithms.title: Selection in Worst-Case Linear Time
algorithms.summary: Median-of-medians pivot guarantees a 30/70 split, so SELECT runs in Θ(n) worst case.

algorithms.title: Weighted Median
algorithms.summary: The element whose lighter side carries < half the total weight, via sorting or linear-time selection.

categories.title: Data Structures
categories.description: Elementary structures, hashing, trees, B-trees, heaps and disjoint sets (Part III).

algorithms.title: Stacks, Queues & Deques
algorithms.summary: Array-based stack, circular queue and deque with overflow/underflow detection; queue from two stacks.

algorithms.title: Linked Lists
algorithms.summary: Doubly linked list with a sentinel (LIST-SEARCH, LIST-INSERT, LIST-DELETE) plus in-place reversal of a singly linked list.

algorithms.title: Implementing Pointers and Objects
algorithms.summary: Multiple-array list representation with a free list: ALLOCATE-OBJECT / FREE-OBJECT, plus compaction.

algorithms.title: Representing Rooted Trees
algorithms.summary: Left-child/right-sibling trees, stack-based and O(1)-space tree traversals.

algorithms.title: Direct-Address Tables & Bit Vectors
algorithms.summary: An array indexed by key: O(1) search/insert/delete when the universe is small; bit-vector sets.

algorithms.title: Hash Tables with Chaining
algorithms.summary: Resolve collisions with linked lists per slot; expected Θ(1+α) per operation under simple uniform hashing.

algorithms.title: Hash Functions & Universal Hashing
algorithms.summary: Division, multiplication and universal hashing methods; string keys as radix-128 integers.

algorithms.title: Open Addressing
algorithms.summary: Store all keys in the table itself; linear probing, quadratic probing and double hashing.

algorithms.title: Perfect Hashing (FKS)
algorithms.summary: Two-level universal hashing gives worst-case O(1) lookup for a static key set in O(n) space.

algorithms.title: Binary Search Trees
algorithms.summary: Inorder walk, search, min/max, successor/predecessor, insert and delete (TRANSPLANT) in O(h).

algorithms.title: Randomly Built Binary Search Trees
algorithms.summary: Inserting keys in random order gives expected height O(lg n); empirical check against the closed forms.

algorithms.title: Red-Black Trees
algorithms.summary: Self-balancing BST: rotations, RB-INSERT and RB-DELETE with fix-up keep height ≤ 2 lg(n+1).

algorithms.title: Order-Statistic Trees
algorithms.summary: Red-black tree augmented with subtree sizes: OS-SELECT and OS-RANK in O(lg n).

algorithms.title: Interval Trees
algorithms.summary: Red-black tree keyed by low endpoints and augmented with the maximum high endpoint: INTERVAL-SEARCH in O(lg n).

algorithms.title: AVL Trees
algorithms.summary: The original height-balanced BST: |height(left) − height(right)| ≤ 1 restored by rotations.

algorithms.title: Treaps
algorithms.summary: BST on keys, heap on random priorities: a randomly built tree regardless of insertion order.

algorithms.title: B-Trees
algorithms.summary: Disk-friendly multiway search trees: split-on-the-way-down insertion and full deletion with merge/borrow.

algorithms.title: Fibonacci Heaps
algorithms.summary: Mergeable heap with amortised O(1) insert, union and decrease-key and O(lg n) extract-min.

algorithms.title: van Emde Boas Trees
algorithms.summary: Priority queue on integers 0..u with insert, delete, member, min/max, successor and predecessor in O(lg lg u).

algorithms.title: Binomial Heaps
algorithms.summary: Mergeable heap built from binomial trees: UNION in O(lg n) by "binary addition" of root lists.

algorithms.title: Disjoint-Set Union (Union-Find)
algorithms.summary: Linked-list sets with weighted union and disjoint-set forests with union by rank + path compression.

categories.title: Advanced Design & Analysis
categories.description: Dynamic programming, greedy algorithms and amortized analysis (Part IV).

algorithms.title: Rod Cutting
algorithms.summary: The introductory dynamic program: naive recursion, memoization, bottom-up and solution reconstruction.

algorithms.title: Assembly-Line Scheduling
algorithms.summary: The original DP example: fastest way through a two-line factory with transfer costs.

algorithms.title: Matrix-Chain Multiplication
algorithms.summary: Choose the parenthesization minimising scalar multiplications: Θ(n³) DP.

algorithms.title: Longest Common Subsequence
algorithms.summary: Θ(mn) dynamic program with table reconstruction and Θ(min(m,n))-space length computation.

algorithms.title: Optimal Binary Search Trees
algorithms.summary: Minimise expected search cost given key and miss probabilities: O(n³) DP, O(n²) with Knuth's monotonicity.

algorithms.title: Longest Palindromic Subsequence
algorithms.summary: The longest subsequence that reads the same forwards and backwards: Θ(n²).

algorithms.title: Edit Distance
algorithms.summary: Transform x into y with copy / replace / delete / insert / twiddle / kill at minimum cost.

algorithms.title: Longest Monotonically Increasing Subsequence
algorithms.summary: O(n²) dynamic program and O(n lg n) patience-sorting variant using binary search.

algorithms.title: 0-1 Knapsack
algorithms.summary: Pseudo-polynomial dynamic program O(nW) for items that cannot be split.

algorithms.title: Bitonic Euclidean Traveling Salesman
algorithms.summary: The shortest bitonic closed tour of points sorted by x, found in O(n²) by DP.

algorithms.title: Printing Neatly
algorithms.summary: Break a paragraph into lines minimising the sum of cubes of trailing blanks: DP over line breaks.

algorithms.title: Optimal Polygon Triangulation
algorithms.summary: Minimum-weight triangulation of a convex polygon: the matrix-chain structure in geometry.

algorithms.title: Image Compression by Seam Carving
algorithms.summary: Find the vertical seam of minimum total disruption in an m×n grid: O(mn) DP.

algorithms.title: More DP: Company Party & Viterbi
algorithms.summary: Planning a company party (tree DP, maximum independent set) and Viterbi decoding of a speech-recognition graph.

algorithms.title: Activity Selection
algorithms.summary: Greedy choice (earliest finish time) picks a maximum set of compatible activities; compared with the DP.

algorithms.title: Fractional Knapsack
algorithms.summary: Greedy by value-per-pound is optimal when items may be split.

algorithms.title: Huffman Codes
algorithms.summary: Optimal prefix-free codes by greedily merging the two least frequent symbols.

algorithms.title: Matroids & Weighted Greedy
algorithms.summary: The matroid greedy algorithm and its instances: maximum spanning tree and unit-time task scheduling with penalties.

algorithms.title: Coin Changing
algorithms.summary: Greedy change-making is optimal for powers of c, but not for arbitrary denominations; DP always works.

algorithms.title: Amortized Analysis: Binary Counter
algorithms.summary: k-bit counter INCREMENT: aggregate, accounting and potential methods give 2 amortized flips per increment.

algorithms.title: Amortized Analysis: Stack with MULTIPOP
algorithms.summary: PUSH, POP and MULTIPOP(k) all cost O(1) amortized: a stack object pays for its own removal.

algorithms.title: Amortized Analysis: Dynamic Tables
algorithms.summary: Doubling on overflow and halving at load 1/4 gives O(1) amortized INSERT and DELETE.

categories.title: Graph Algorithms
categories.description: Traversals, spanning trees, shortest paths, flows and matchings (Part VI).

algorithms.title: Graph Representations
algorithms.summary: Adjacency lists and matrices, transposing a graph, squaring a graph, and the O(V) universal-sink test.

algorithms.title: Breadth-First Search
algorithms.summary: Level-by-level traversal: shortest paths (in edges) from a source, bipartiteness test and tree diameter.

algorithms.title: Depth-First Search
algorithms.summary: Discovery/finish timestamps, parenthesis structure and tree/back/forward/cross edge classification.

algorithms.title: Topological Sort
algorithms.summary: Linearly order a DAG's vertices by decreasing DFS finish time, or by repeatedly removing sources (Kahn).

algorithms.title: Strongly Connected Components
algorithms.summary: Kosaraju's two-pass DFS (CLRS) and Tarjan's one-pass algorithm; the component DAG.

algorithms.title: Articulation Points, Bridges & Biconnected Components
algorithms.summary: Low-link DFS finds cut vertices, bridges and the biconnected components of an undirected graph in Θ(V+E).

algorithms.title: Euler Tours
algorithms.summary: Closed walks using every edge exactly once (Hierholzer), for directed and undirected graphs.

algorithms.title: Kruskal's Minimum Spanning Tree
algorithms.summary: Sort edges by weight and add each that joins two components (union-find); second-best MST.

algorithms.title: Prim's Minimum Spanning Tree
algorithms.summary: Grow one tree from a root, always adding the lightest edge leaving it (min-priority queue).

algorithms.title: Bellman-Ford Single-Source Shortest Paths
algorithms.summary: Relax every edge V−1 times; detects reachable negative-weight cycles. O(VE).

algorithms.title: Shortest Paths in a DAG
algorithms.summary: Relax edges in topological order: Θ(V+E) even with negative weights; longest paths and critical paths.

algorithms.title: Dijkstra's Algorithm
algorithms.summary: Greedy single-source shortest paths for non-negative weights, using a min-priority queue.

algorithms.title: Difference Constraints
algorithms.summary: Solve systems xⱼ − xᵢ ≤ w by shortest paths in a constraint graph (Bellman-Ford).

algorithms.title: Floyd-Warshall All-Pairs Shortest Paths
algorithms.summary: Θ(V³) dynamic program over intermediate vertices; also transitive closure (Warshall).

algorithms.title: Johnson's Algorithm
algorithms.summary: All-pairs shortest paths on sparse graphs: reweight with Bellman-Ford potentials, then run Dijkstra from every vertex.

algorithms.title: APSP by Matrix Multiplication
algorithms.summary: Shortest paths via (min,+) matrix products: SLOW-ALL-PAIRS Θ(V⁴), FASTER-ALL-PAIRS Θ(V³ lg V).

algorithms.title: Ford-Fulkerson & Edmonds-Karp Maximum Flow
algorithms.summary: Augment along residual paths: DFS (Ford-Fulkerson) or BFS shortest paths (Edmonds-Karp, O(VE²)); min-cut extraction.

algorithms.title: Push-Relabel & Relabel-to-Front
algorithms.summary: Preflow-push maximum flow: generic O(V²E) and relabel-to-front O(V³).

algorithms.title: Maximum Bipartite Matching via Flow
algorithms.summary: Reduce matching to max flow with unit capacities; integrality gives a maximum matching in O(VE).

algorithms.title: Hopcroft-Karp Matching
algorithms.summary: Find many shortest vertex-disjoint augmenting paths per phase: O(E√V) maximum bipartite matching.

algorithms.title: Hungarian Algorithm (Assignment Problem)
algorithms.summary: Minimum-cost perfect matching in a complete bipartite graph in O(n³) using vertex potentials.

algorithms.title: Stable Matching (Gale-Shapley)
algorithms.summary: Propose-and-reject deferred acceptance yields a stable marriage in O(n²) — optimal for the proposing side.

algorithms.title: Minimum Mean-Weight Cycle (Karp)
algorithms.summary: Karp's O(VE) algorithm: min over v of max over k of (d_n(v) − d_k(v))/(n − k).

algorithms.title: Parallel Fibonacci & Work-Span Analysis
algorithms.summary: spawn/sync Fibonacci, with work T₁, span T∞ and parallelism T₁/T∞ computed from the computation DAG.

algorithms.title: Parallel Matrix Multiplication
algorithms.summary: P-MAT-VEC and P-SQUARE-MATRIX-MULTIPLY with parallel loops; recursive divide-and-conquer with spawn.

algorithms.title: Parallel Merge Sort
algorithms.summary: Parallel merge via binary search on the median of the longer array: span Θ(lg³ n), parallelism Θ(n/lg² n).

algorithms.title: List Ranking (Pointer Jumping)
algorithms.summary: Compute every node's distance to the end of a linked list in O(lg n) PRAM steps by repeated pointer doubling.

algorithms.title: Parallel Prefix (Scan)
algorithms.summary: All prefix sums in ⌈lg n⌉ steps (recursive doubling) or with O(n) work (up-sweep / down-sweep).

algorithms.title: Constant-Time Maximum on a CRCW PRAM
algorithms.summary: With n² processors and concurrent writes, find the maximum in O(1); contrast with the Θ(lg n) EREW tree.

algorithms.title: Euler-Tour Technique on Trees
algorithms.summary: Compute every vertex's depth in O(lg n) PRAM time by listing the Euler tour and running a parallel prefix over ±1.

categories.title: Arithmetic Circuits
categories.description: Adders, multipliers and clocked circuits (1st edition).

algorithms.title: Combinational Circuits
algorithms.summary: A gate-level circuit model with size and depth: the building block for adders and multipliers.

algorithms.title: Ripple-Carry Adder
algorithms.summary: n cascaded full adders: simple, Θ(n) size, but Θ(n) depth because the carry ripples.

algorithms.title: Carry-Lookahead Adder
algorithms.summary: Compute all carries with a parallel-prefix network over (generate, propagate) pairs: Θ(lg n) depth.

algorithms.title: Carry-Save Adder
algorithms.summary: Reduce three n-bit numbers to two in constant depth (a row of independent full adders).

algorithms.title: Array & Wallace-Tree Multipliers
algorithms.summary: Multiply n-bit numbers: array multiplier with ripple adders (Θ(n) depth) vs carry-save Wallace tree (Θ(lg n) depth).

algorithms.title: Clocked Circuits: Bit-Serial Arithmetic
algorithms.summary: Sequential circuits with registers: a one-full-adder serial adder (n cycles) and a shift-and-add multiplier.

categories.title: Matrix Operations
categories.description: LUP decomposition, inversion and least squares.

algorithms.title: LU and LUP Decomposition
algorithms.summary: Solve Ax = b by factoring PA = LU with partial pivoting, then forward/back substitution in Θ(n³).

algorithms.title: Matrix Inversion
algorithms.summary: Invert a matrix by solving n systems with one LUP factorisation; equivalent in difficulty to matrix multiplication.

algorithms.title: Symmetric Positive-Definite Matrices & Least Squares
algorithms.summary: Cholesky factorisation of SPD matrices and curve fitting by the normal equations AᵀA c = Aᵀy.

algorithms.title: The Simplex Algorithm & Duality
algorithms.summary: Maximise cᵀx subject to Ax ≤ b, x ≥ 0 by pivoting between basic feasible solutions; initialisation and LP duality.

categories.title: Polynomials & FFT
categories.description: Fast Fourier transform and polynomial arithmetic.

algorithms.title: Fast Fourier Transform (Recursive)
algorithms.summary: RECURSIVE-FFT evaluates a polynomial at the n complex n-th roots of unity in Θ(n lg n); the inverse DFT interpolates.

algorithms.title: Iterative FFT (Bit-Reversal Butterflies)
algorithms.summary: BIT-REVERSE-COPY then lg n in-place butterfly passes: the loop structure used by hardware FFT circuits.

algorithms.title: Polynomial Multiplication via FFT
algorithms.summary: Multiply two degree-n polynomials in Θ(n lg n): evaluate with FFT, multiply pointwise, interpolate with the inverse FFT.

algorithms.title: Polynomial Evaluation & Lagrange Interpolation
algorithms.summary: Recover coefficients from n point-value pairs in Θ(n²) using Lagrange's formula; evaluate with Horner.

categories.title: Number-Theoretic Algorithms
categories.description: GCD, modular arithmetic, RSA and primality.

algorithms.title: Euclid's GCD Algorithm
algorithms.summary: gcd(a, b) = gcd(b, a mod b): O(lg b) steps (Lamé's theorem); plus binary GCD and lcm.

algorithms.title: Extended Euclid & Modular Inverses
algorithms.summary: EXTENDED-EUCLID finds x, y with ax + by = gcd(a,b) (Bézout); gives modular inverses.

algorithms.title: Modular Linear Equations
algorithms.summary: Solve ax ≡ b (mod n): d = gcd(a, n) solutions mod n if d | b, none otherwise.

algorithms.title: Chinese Remainder Theorem
algorithms.summary: Reconstruct x mod n₁n₂…n_k from residues modulo pairwise coprime moduli; also merging non-coprime congruences.

algorithms.title: Modular Exponentiation
algorithms.summary: a^b mod n by repeated squaring in O(β) multiplications; powers, orders and primitive roots.

algorithms.title: Modular Groups & Euler's Totient
algorithms.summary: The group Z_n*, Euler's φ(n), subgroups generated by an element, and Euler's/Fermat's theorems.

algorithms.title: Primality Testing: Fermat & Miller-Rabin
algorithms.summary: The pseudoprimality test (fooled by Carmichael numbers) and the randomized Miller-Rabin test with error ≤ 2^−s.

algorithms.title: RSA Public-Key Cryptosystem
algorithms.summary: Key generation from two primes, encryption/decryption by modular exponentiation, and signatures.

algorithms.title: Pollard's Rho Integer Factorization
algorithms.summary: Find a factor of n in expected O(n^¼) steps by detecting a cycle of x ↦ x²+c mod n.

algorithms.title: Naive String Matching
algorithms.summary: Slide the pattern over the text one position at a time: Θ((n−m+1)m).

algorithms.title: Rabin-Karp Algorithm
algorithms.summary: Compare rolling hashes of the pattern and each text window; verify hash hits. Expected Θ(n + m).

algorithms.title: String Matching with Finite Automata
algorithms.summary: Build the string-matching automaton δ(q, a) in O(m|Σ|) and scan the text in Θ(n).

algorithms.title: Knuth-Morris-Pratt Algorithm
algorithms.summary: The prefix function π lets the matcher never move backwards in the text: Θ(n + m) with O(m) space.

algorithms.title: Boyer-Moore Algorithm
algorithms.summary: Scan the pattern right to left; bad-character and good-suffix heuristics skip text positions: sublinear in practice.

algorithms.title: Suffix Arrays & LCP Arrays
algorithms.summary: Sorted array of all suffixes (prefix doubling) with Kasai's LCP array: substring search in O(m lg n).

algorithms.title: Line-Segment Properties & Intersection
algorithms.summary: Cross products decide turn direction and whether two segments intersect, using only integer arithmetic.

algorithms.title: Sweep Line: Do Any Two Segments Intersect?
algorithms.summary: Shamos-Hoey sweep: keep segments ordered by y along a moving vertical line and test only neighbours: O(n lg n) probes.

algorithms.title: Convex Hull: Graham's Scan
algorithms.summary: Sort points by polar angle around the lowest point, then discard non-left turns with a stack: O(n lg n).

algorithms.title: Convex Hull: Jarvis's March
algorithms.summary: Gift wrapping: from each hull vertex pick the point with the smallest polar angle; output-sensitive O(nh).

algorithms.title: Closest Pair of Points
algorithms.summary: Divide and conquer on x with a y-sorted strip: only 7 comparisons per point, O(n lg n).

algorithms.title: NP Verification Algorithms
algorithms.summary: Polynomial-time verifiers for Hamiltonian cycle, clique, vertex cover, CNF-SAT and subset sum — the definition of NP.

algorithms.title: Hamiltonian Cycle & Exact TSP
algorithms.summary: Exponential exact algorithms: backtracking search, and the Held-Karp O(n²2ⁿ) dynamic program for tours.

algorithms.title: Satisfiability: Brute Force, DPLL and 2-SAT
algorithms.summary: SAT is NP-complete; compare exhaustive search, DPLL backtracking with unit propagation, and linear-time 2-SAT via SCCs.

algorithms.title: Polynomial-Time Reductions
algorithms.summary: 3-CNF-SAT ≤ₚ CLIQUE ≤ₚ VERTEX-COVER and HAM-CYCLE ≤ₚ TSP, implemented as instance transformations and tested for equivalence.

algorithms.title: Subset Sum
algorithms.summary: NP-complete in the input length yet solvable in O(nt) pseudo-polynomial time; meet-in-the-middle O(2^{n/2}).

categories.title: Approximation Algorithms
categories.description: Provable near-optimal algorithms for hard problems.

algorithms.title: Approximate Vertex Cover
algorithms.summary: Take both endpoints of a maximal matching: a polynomial-time 2-approximation.

algorithms.title: Approximate Metric TSP
algorithms.summary: Preorder walk of a minimum spanning tree: a 2-approximation when distances satisfy the triangle inequality.

algorithms.title: Greedy Set Cover
algorithms.summary: Repeatedly pick the set covering the most uncovered elements: an H(d)-approximation, H(d) ≤ ln d + 1.

algorithms.title: FPTAS for Subset Sum
algorithms.summary: Trim the list of reachable sums by a factor (1+ε/2n): a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme.

algorithms.title: Weighted Vertex Cover by LP Rounding
algorithms.summary: Solve the LP relaxation (x_u + x_v ≥ 1), then round every x_v ≥ ½ up: a 2-approximation for weighted cover.

algorithms.title: Randomized Approximation: MAX-3-CNF & MAX-CUT
algorithms.summary: A random assignment satisfies 7/8 of clauses in expectation; derandomise with conditional expectations.

categories.title: Machine Learning
categories.description: Clustering, weighted majority, gradient descent (4th edition).

algorithms.title: k-Means Clustering (Lloyd's Algorithm)
algorithms.summary: Alternate between assigning points to the nearest center and moving centers to cluster means; cost never increases.

algorithms.title: Weighted-Majority Algorithm
algorithms.summary: Learning from expert advice: shrink the weight of every wrong expert by (1−ε); mistakes ≤ 2(1+ε)m + (2 ln n)/ε.

algorithms.title: Gradient Descent
algorithms.summary: Minimise a differentiable convex function by repeatedly stepping against the gradient; linear regression example.

categories.title: Online Algorithms
categories.description: Competitive analysis, caching, self-organising lists (4th edition).

algorithms.title: Waiting for an Elevator (Competitive Analysis)
algorithms.summary: Wait up to the cost of the stairs, then walk: a deterministic 2-competitive online strategy (ski rental).

algorithms.title: Self-Organizing Lists: Move-to-Front
algorithms.summary: Access cost = position; moving each accessed item to the front is 4-competitive against any strategy.

algorithms.title: Online Caching: LRU, FIFO and Belady's Optimum
algorithms.summary: Cache replacement policies compared by cache misses; LRU and FIFO are k-competitive, furthest-in-future is optimal offline.
